newsitem.title: JORDAN: Accused killer of Israeli girls beaten up -defence.
newsitem.headline: Accused killer of Israeli girls beaten up -defence.

text.p: Lawyers defending a Jordanian soldier charged with shooting seven Israeli schoolgirls told a military court on Saturday their client had been beaten by his guards while in prison.

Defence lawyer Hussein Mjalli said Private Ahmed Daqamsa was attacked by officers at the high security detention centre in Amman where he has been held since the March shooting on a northern border post.
But the prosecution denied his claim.
"The defendant has not been subjected to any beating and this is a theatrical attempt and a cheap ploy by the defence," said chief prosecutor Muhanad Hijazi.
Hijazi asked for a doctor to examine the bruises, which he said were self-inflicted and followed an attempt by Daqamsa to escape after leaving his cell to go to the toilet.
Earlier Daqamsa, with visible bruises on his face, showed his defence lawyer from his cage in the dock swollen red marks on his shoulder.

Chief Judge Brigadier Mamoun al-Khasawneh agreed to a defence request to postpone the defendant's testimony until next Wednesday to give more time for completion of a medical report on Daqamsa's mental state.
Daqamsa has not denied shooting the girls, six of them 13 years old and one just 11, but says he acted impulsively after being provoked during Moslem prayers.
He is charged with premeditated murder and faces the death sentence if found guilty. The prosecution say he had been planning to kill Israelis for many years.
